newsitem.title: UK: Algeria's Sonatrach outlines LPG development plans.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's Sonatrach outlines LPG development plans.

text.p: An official of Algerian state energy company Sonatrach on Wednesday outlined the firm's plans to double liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) production, and more than double exports, by 2005.
Ali Benbouzid told a conference that the huge extra volumes will come from continued development of the vast Hassi R'mel field, with proven reserves of 2,500 billion cubic metres of natural gas.
This is around 70 percent of Algeria's total gas reserves.
Benbouzid, an official in Sonatrach's international sales department, said more than 80 percent of Algeria's LPG comes from natural gas processing.

LPG production is set to rise to 8.8 million tonnes in 2000 before peaking at 10.5 million tonnes in 2005. As fields mature, there will be a gradual decline, with output expected to slip to 10.0 million tonnes in 2015.
This compares with stable output of around five million tonnes a year between 1991 and 1995, Benbouzid said.

This huge extra volume will far exceed Algeria's current processing capacity, which stands at six million tonnes a year in plants at Arzew and Bethioua. But these are now being revamped and capacity will increase to 8.4 million tonnes a year by 1998.

The pipeline network will also need to be extended. The 24-inch Hassi R'mel-Arzew pipeline will have its capacity expanded to nine million tonnes a year from the current six million by the addition of extra boosting facilities.
Exports will rise as production is set to grow far more than domestic consumption.

Benbouzid said current LPG consumption -- 94 percent of which is butane in cylinders -- has been stable at 1.5 million tonnes a year for each of the last five years. This is equivalent to 54 kg per head of population, one of the highest levels in Africa.
Assuming a growth rate of three percent a year, and excluding petrochemical use, Benbouzid expects consumption to rise to 1.7 million tonnes by 2000, and to 2.7 million tonnes by 2015.
And with production rising so much faster than consumption, exports will grow to a peak of 8.5 million tonnes a year from the steady level of 3.5 million tonnes over the last five years.

Sonatrach currently sells to 20 countries, of which the Mediterranean, with 54 percent of all sales, the U.S. with 21 percent and Brazil with 10 percent are the most important markets. The company intends to continue selling the same percentages as output grows.

With such a huge increase in the volume of LPG coming onto the market -- a speaker from Total told the conference that global LPG trade will only be 48 million tonnes in 2000 -- Sonatrach faces questions of whether it will be able to sell the new tonnes.
Benbouzid was confident, saying that new markets such as power generation and air conditioning as well as transport are all introducing LPG to new markets.
"Booming electricity demand in countries where natural gas is not available is particularly exciting," he said.
